title: Can feminism meet the challenges of 2026?
gist: Alona Ferber reviews Natasha Walter's Feminism for a World on Fire, which argues feminism lost its way to consumer capitalism, growth obsession and individual 'ladder-climbing' aspiration and must fuse with the climate struggle; Ferber credits its diagnosis and nuanced handling of trans-rights splits but finds its prescriptions thin and its climate-feminism link more correlation than causation.

insights.claim: Natasha Walter's central thesis is that feminism lost its way under consumer capitalism, the mirage of endless growth and individual success, shifting from dismantling hierarchies to women climbing 'a kind of ladder'.
